messages:
ana: heads up — perf dashboard shows a sharp drop in prefix cache hit rate after last night's runtime deploy (kernel selector bump + new encrypted keying). :eyes:
jordan: saw the chart, pretty dramatic. numbers?
mike: raw numbers from the job: pre-upgrade global_hit_rate=0.63, post-upgrade=0.13. several high-traffic tenants went from 70% -> ~10%.
sophia: wow. did the deploy touch normalization or key derivation code?
ana: (typo) ana: the only obvious changes were kernel selector heuristics and switching cache keys to be encrypted with per-tenant wrapping (RFC-1888 style). no explicit prompt normalization changes.
jordan: infra-bot ran a quick diff of generated keys and found ordering differences in serialized KV blobs between kernels. that might change the input to the HMAC before encryption.
infra-bot: artifact: kernel-3.4.1 -> kernel-3.5.0 changed struct packing for the prefix frame; MD5(hash_input) positions shifted by 8 bytes.
mike: if serialization order shifted, then the HMAC->nonce sequence might produce entirely different ciphertexts for identical logical keys -> miss. but that shouldn't cause cross-tenant collisions.
sophia: security note — our encrypted keying uses tenant_id only as an associated_data (AEAD) and not inside the plaintext key material. if AEAD verification fails we drop the entry and treat as miss. need to confirm we didn't accidentally drop tenant_id for some requests.
sec-team: quick check — logs show ~0.4% of cache writes missing tenant header after the RPC middleware update. suspicious.
jordan: aha, middleware change was rolled in an unrelated PR last week. could be a small fraction of writes lacking tenant binding -> entries created with empty AAD. readers with proper AAD will see HMAC mismatch -> miss, writers/reads mismatch.
mike: reproduce script running. small repro: create two tenants tA/tB, write identical prompt. with missing AAD we get same ciphertext for both tenants (because AAD not included) -> potential cross-tenant exposure if ciphertexts are stored in shared cache without tenant namespace.
sophia: that's the scary part: we namespace keys by tenant in the KVS, but we also store encrypted key blobs that include metadata. if namespace and blob-level AAD disagree, you can end up with same blob referenced in multiple namespaces via aliasing bug in cache index. need to audit aliasing code.
nana: ana: snippet from cache key derivation (simplified):
```python
def make_cache_blob(prompt, tenant_id, salt):
    normal = normalize_prompt(prompt)
    key_material = sha256(salt + normal.encode())[:16]
    # tenant_id used as AAD in AEAD encrypt
    ct = aead_encrypt(key_material, aad=tenant_id.encode(), key=wrap_key)
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(ct)
```

mike: if tenant_id.encode() is empty, ct depends only on key_material -> same across tenants that missed tenant header.
jordan: mitigation plan: (1) patch RPC middleware to reject writes without tenant header (fast), (2) add a guard in cache write path to append tenant namespace into the plaintext blob as a last-resort, (3) backfill audit to find blobs with >1 tenant references.
sophia: also recommend we emit per-tenant hit-rate metrics (histogram) and a collision detector that samples blobs and maps them to tenant ids to find shared blobs.
sec-team: agree. add immediate alert for any blob referenced by >1 tenant_id. we should treat that as potential exposure and rotate wrap keys for affected tenants.
mike: running reproducer now, will produce a dump of suspect blob ids in ~15m.
nana: ana: quick perf thought — kernel change also changed serialization padding which increases key_material entropy distribution, so some previously-frequent matches might now hash differently even with correct AAD. need to separate miss causes: serialization mismatch vs missing AAD vs pure keying logic.
jordan: good point. instrument two binary flags in metrics on miss: miss_reason=serialization_delta | miss_reason=bad_aad | miss_reason=hash_mismatch. we can log sampled pre-image and compare.
infra-bot: perf-profiling job queued: prefix-cache-sample-compare-1934567890. will run across canary + prod snapshots and produce diff. ETA 2h.
mike: immediate rollback option: revert kernel selector on canary to restore old serialization. i'll prepare PR to pin kernel on canary and watch hit-rate.
sophia: can we hot-fix the middleware to stop new bad writes ASAP? that should reduce ongoing contamination while we investigate root cause.
jordan: I'll own the canary rollback. mike takes middleware hotfix. sophia coordinates sec response and backfill. ana will draft incident note for all-hands.
sec-team: also request: full audit log export for writes between 1934460000-1934567890 for the cache index. we need write-level evidence.
mike: got reproducer partial results: in sample 10k writes, 42 had empty tenant header, those produced 37 unique blobs referenced by multiple namespaces. exporting list to s3://redwood-internal/tmp/kv-collisions-1934567890.csv
ana: ana: thanks — putting this in follow-up thread. can we also run a quick calculation of exposure surface: how many embeddings/keys correspond to PII prompts? (PD teams)
sophia: I'll ask data-protection team to prioritize sampling.
jordan: TL;DR action items: rollback kernel on canary (jordan), hotfix middleware to reject missing tenant header (mike), run blob-to-tenant collision detector and generate list (mike+infra-bot), run sec backfill & key rotation plan for affected tenants (sophia+sec-team), add per-tenant hit metrics and miss_reason tagging (ana+eng-metrics).
nana: ana: noted. we'll track as a hot incident. ping if you need help with canary dashboards. :thumbsup:
